---
title: "3 · Relaxation and MD"
---

`sample.py` processes each starting configuration with its assigned generator
(step 1) and saves several frames from it. All calculations use float32, a fixed
cell and periodic boundaries in all directions.

## Relaxation

ASE FIRE runs to a maximum force of 0.05 eV/Å or 200 steps. The saved frames are
the starting structure, the structures at steps 3, 10, 30 and 80 when the
optimiser reaches them, and the final structure. The early steps keep the
strained, curved and freshly defected geometries before they relax, and the
final structure gives the generator's local minimum.

## MD

Half of the configurations, chosen at random, continue from the relaxed
structure into Langevin MD at fixed cell: 600 fs at a 1 fs time step (0.5 fs
when H is present) with friction 0.02 fs⁻¹. The temperature is 300 K (25 %),
600 K (20 %), 1000 K (20 %), 1500 K (20 %) or 2000 K (15 %), with velocities
drawn from the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution. A frame is saved every 20 fs
after the first 100 fs, giving 26 frames per run. A run stops early if a force
exceeds 50 eV/Å, a position or force becomes non-finite, or two atoms come
within 0.7 Å.

## Filtering

`assemble.py` gathers all frames and removes a frame when:

- two atoms are closer than 1.0 Å (0.8 Å for pairs with one H, 0.6 Å for H–H);
- any atom has no neighbour within 2.3 Å, which catches desorbed or detached
  atoms;
- the generator's largest force exceeds 30 eV/Å.

## Results

The five generators processed all 1,300 configurations in about 2 h 15 min of
wall time, from 01:39 to 03:24. Between 92 % and 98 % of relaxations reached
0.05 eV/Å within 200 FIRE steps; the rest still contribute their saved steps. No
MD run hit the stopping criteria. Filtering removed 53 of 23,784 frames, almost
all because an adatom or a small fragment had detached.

When PET finished, a second MatterSim worker started from the end of
MatterSim's list. The first worker was already running an earlier version of
`sample.py` without the check for configurations finished by another worker, so
it recomputed 58 configurations. Both runs use the same random seeds, the later
file replaced the earlier one, and the tables count each configuration once.
